newsitem.title: USA: NICOR unit to withdraw rate proposal.
newsitem.headline: NICOR unit to withdraw rate proposal.

text.p: Northern Illinois Gas, a unit of NICOR Inc, said Thursday it intends to withdraw a performance-based rate proposal that it filed with the Illinois Commerce Commission in August, 1996.
The company said it filed the proposal in response to an amendment to the Illinois Public Utilities Act, which authorized the commission to approve performance-based rates on an experimental basis.

Under the proposed program, Northern Illinois Gas would have compared its total annual gas supply costs against a market-based benchmark, and the difference would have been shared between the company and its customers.
Currently, natural gas supply costs are recovered directly from customers without mark-up.
When the plan was filed, Northern Illinois Gas said, the company believed that it and its customers could benefit from a plan that moved toward market-based pricing.

Northern Illinois Gas said the legislation that authorizes the commission to approve performance-based rates contains language that can be interpreted to require standards that it says are nearly impossible to achieve, particularly in the case of experimental programs.
The company said that when it filed its proposal it recognized that a successful outcome in its rate case depended on a change, either in legislative language or its interpretation by the commission.
"Since neither has happened, the company has reluctantly concluded that a performance-based rate program is not feasible under Illinois law at this time," Northern Illinois Gas said in a statement.
Withdrawal of the plan will not impact Northern Illinois Gas' existing rates or operations, it said.
